asked: Please state the verification for the anchor: from a reference date you can justify (e.g., 2025-01-01 or 2026-03-01), give the day count to 2026-01-01 and the mod-7 result showing it is Thursday. Also confirm 2026 is treated as a non-leap year and say where that matters.

For the four dates closest to a weekend boundary (2026-06-22, 2026-06-23, 2026-05-25, 2026-06-12), state each computed weekday and whether an off-by-one in the anchor would flip any of them into Saturday or Sunday.
replies:
Anchor verification: Use 2025-01-01, which is a well-known Wednesday (Jan 1, 2025). 2025 is a non-leap year (365 days), so 2026-01-01 is 365 days later. 365 mod 7 = 1, so 2026-01-01 is Wednesday + 1 = Thursday. This confirms the anchor. 2026 is a non-leap year because 2026 is not divisible by 4 (2026/4 = 506.5). This matters for day-of-year calculations after February: February has 28 days, so dates from March onward are shifted one day earlier relative to a leap-year calendar. For example, 2026-03-01 is day 60, not day 61.

Boundary dates check:
2026-06-22: day 173, (173-1) mod 7 = 172 mod 7 = 4 → Monday. Off-by-one anchor would make it Sunday (flips into weekend).
2026-06-23: day 174, (174-1) mod 7 = 173 mod 7 = 5 → Tuesday. Off-by-one anchor would make it Monday (no flip).
2026-05-25: day 145, (145-1) mod 7 = 144 mod 7 = 4 → Monday. Off-by-one anchor would make it Sunday (flips into weekend).
2026-06-12: day 163, (163-1) mod 7 = 162 mod 7 = 1 → Friday. Off-by-one anchor would make it Thursday (no flip).

So an off-by-one anchor error would incorrectly add 2026-06-22 and 2026-05-25 as weekend dates, changing the count from 4 to 6. The original answer's weekend dates (2026-06-20, 2026-05-16, 2026-05-17, 2026-06-07) are all correct, and the count of 4 is correct.
